grade.first_issue: After correctly reducing the goal to a dot-product identity, the submission merely calls that identity “a trigonometric identity” and invokes unspecified symmetry; it never derives the required compatibility among B, C, K, and L. This is an unsupported central inference under Rule E, so the score is capped at 3.
grade.summary: The coordinate reduction and several sine-law relations are useful preliminary work, but the entire load-bearing step proving the target dot-product identity is absent. The purported circumcentre formula is unfinished, and the final coordinate/line assertion uses undefined objects and is not a proof that O lies on the perpendicular bisector of MN. Rule B does not permit a score of 4 because no complete parameter reduction, angle-domain treatment, or explicit final calculation is supplied.
strengths: Correctly expresses M and N after taking A as the origin.
Correctly records the circumcentre equations 2O·k=|k|² and 2O·l=|l|².
The sine-law calculations leading to the cotangent relations are largely valid and constitute relevant preliminary progress.

errors.description: The essential dot-product identity is asserted from “symmetry” without any derivation. No argument connects the obtained angle relations and length equations to this identity.
The displayed formula for O contains an undefined vector n, has both terms in the same direction, and is left with an ellipsis; it cannot be used to compute the required dot product.

The concluding statement about an x-component and a line through the midpoint of AP uses an undefined point P and an unspecified coordinate direction. It neither establishes nor correctly identifies the perpendicular bisector of MN.
The transformations through tangent expressions do not address cases where one of the relevant tangents is undefined, although the final cotangent relations could instead be derived directly.
